title: Shell Mastery and Scripting
teachingRule: Explain in fifth-grade reading language, keep technical details exact, define jargon immediately, and connect every idea to production and interviews.
coreIdeas: Use set -euo pipefail so scripts stop on errors, reject missing variables, and fail when any pipeline step fails.
Use EXIT traps to clean temporary files, containers, locks, and partial state.
Use getopts for standard command-line flags such as -n and -d.
Use timestamped logs so a future operator can understand what happened.
Use small tests with fake input and expected output before trusting a script in production.
buildExercise: Build safe-rotate.sh, a 200-line log rotation tool. It should keep the last five copies, gzip older copies, refuse to run as root, use set -euo pipefail, an EXIT trap, getopts, timestamped logs, and tests/test_rotate.sh.
steps: Write the strict header and empty main
Create and clean a staging file
Rotate, truncate, shift, delete, and gzip safely
Test with a temporary directory and fake logs
interviewAngle: A senior FDE should explain failure modes, cleanup, observability, idempotency, and evidence, not only Bash syntax.
nextStep: Read chapters 4 through 6 of The Linux Command Line, then convert one daily task into a tested Bash script.
